evidence.quote: The tensile strength of La-TZM alloy prepared by doping the rare earth element La and introducing C is 1666.39 MPa, which is 85.3 % higher than TZM alloy.

The strengthening mechanism of La-TZM alloy is mainly regulated by the Orowan mechanism, where the critical phase transformation size (dC) of the second phase is inversely proportional to the interfacial energy (γ) between the matrix and the second phase.

According to the interaction mechanism between the second phase and the gliding dislocations, two different strengthening mechanisms can be obtained. One is the Orowan mechanism in which the dislocations bypass the second phase and leave dislocation loops around the particles. The other is the cutting mechanism in which the dislocations cut through the second phase.
When the second phase is semi-coherent with the matrix, chemical strengthening plays a major role.

A typical example is the controlled addition of titanium and zirconium in TZM alloy, which induces solid solution strengthening and second phase strengthening, thereby improving the strength of Mo alloy.
In this work, a novel high-strength La-TZM alloy was designed and prepared via multicomponent second phase.

In Fig. 6 and Fig. 7, it can be seen that ZrO2 and La-Ti-Zr-O are not coherent with the Mo matrix. The interplanar spacing of ZrO2 is 0.293 nm, while the interplanar spacing of Mo is 0.1574 nm, and the two have different crystal orientations. In the same way, La-Ti-Zr-O and Mo matrix is in different lattice relationship. And they have different interplanar spacing, with La-Ti-Zr-O at 0.3118 nm and Mo at 0.2228 nm. Therefore, they conform to the Orowan strengthening mechanism.

Microstructure characterization has revealed that most of the second phase particles in La-TZM alloy exceed the critical size, indicating that La-TZM alloy is mainly strengthened through the Orowan mechanism.
The tensile strength of La-TZM alloy prepared by doping the rare earth element La and introducing C is 1666.39 MPa, which is 85.3 % higher than TZM alloy.
